about: Tagout held-out set #2, written Oct 25 2026 and committed, pushed and tagged before any arm runs on it. It is built to measure what the first sets didn't: a household code that is NOT printed verbatim in the recall but sits inside a printed serial range, a prefix-and-number family, or a best-by or use-by window, and near misses that sit just outside one or in the gap of an enumerated lot list (where a range reading would wrongly call them recalled). On Oct 25 no agency database had a record dated Oct 23 or later (CPSC's newest batch is Oct 22, openFDA's newest enforcement report Oct 14, NHTSA's newest relevant campaign Oct 19), so the database cases come from the freshest records that are in no other case file (eval/cases.json, cases-holdout.json, cases-allergen.json): CPSC Sep 3 - Oct 8, openFDA Oct 14. The lag-window cases are an FDA advisory of Oct 23 and an FDA company announcement (page dated Oct 14) that openFDA does not list. Nothing in lib/ was changed with these cases in view. Each line is what a household would type. Ground truth comes from the agency record or the saved notice text, checked by eval/verify-holdout2.mjs with no Tagout code: for range, family and window cases it parses the printed bounds and compares, rather than looking for the household's code as a substring.

sets.database: Recalls already in an API Tagout queries (CPSC, openFDA, NHTSA), not in any other case file.
sets.lag: Recalls no database Tagout queries has: an FDA advisory (Oct 23) and an FDA company announcement with no openFDA report. Only the web search can find these.

probes.range: The household code is inside a printed from-to serial range; the code itself is printed nowhere.
probes.family: The household code is a printed prefix plus a number inside a printed number range.
probes.window: The deciding fact is a date inside (or outside) a printed best-by or use-by window.
probes.gap: The household code sits between two codes of an enumerated list and is printed nowhere: not recalled.
probes.listed: The household code is printed in the recall (the familiar case).
probes.whole-line: A recall or advisory of every unit, which prints no code.
probes.car: A make, model and year with NHTSA campaigns (orange: the VIN decides).
probes.clean: A code no CPSC or FDA record prints.

expect.danger: Red: the unit is covered (its code is printed, or inside a printed range, family or window).
expect.not-danger: Orange or green: the recall doesn't cover it.
expect.flag: Orange or red, never green: a recall of every unit, or one limited by dates the line doesn't settle.
expect.warning: Orange (cars: make, model and year recalled; the VIN decides).
